that does not mean the danger is over.
Here's Regan McCarthy from member station WFSU.
Isaias brought heavy rain to many areas
that were already fairly soaked.
Governor Ron DeSantis says he's expecting to see rivers rise
and flooding in the next few days.
I've been through these storms long enough

you kinda see where it entered,

people have two feet of water in their neighborhood.
DeSantis says crews will be ready to assist
with water rescues if needed.
He's urging caution and reminding drivers
to stay away from flooded roads.
For NPR News, I'm Regan McCarthy in Tallahassee.
The FDA says it won't finish internal research
on the abortion pill Mifapristone until March.
NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports
several Republican-run states have filed lawsuits.
Over 100 studies have shown that Mifapristone
is safe and effective in ending a pregnancy
in its first 10 weeks.
It's been approved by the FDA for more than 25 years,
and the agency says it's been used
by more than 7.5 million patients.
Currently, the FDA allows it to be prescribed remotely
and sent through the mail.
Anti-abortion rights groups
and some state and federal Republican officials
have been pushing hard for the FDA
to restrict access nationally,
including through court cases.
FDA announced last year it would review its safety data.
The agency told a judge
in one of the Mifapristone cases this week
that March is the earliest the report would be ready.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News.

The comments come as Beijing ratchets up military

Lai says that Taiwan's boosting of its defenses

"ensure that dialogue can take place on the basis of parity."
His comments come as the U.S. continues to hold out
on a $14 billion U.S. arms package sale to the island.
Authorities in Beijing have accused Lai
of supporting Taiwanese independence
and exaggerating the threat from China.
For NPR News, I'm Jan Kamisen Brumby in Taipei.
-Police in the U.K. say a man has died today
after he entered the tiger enclosure at a wildlife park.
The incident occurred at the Yorkshire Wildlife Park
near Duncaster in northern England.
Police stress the tigers are still in the enclosure.
There is no danger to the public.
Authorities did not release any information
about the nature of the man's injuries,
although there is some gruesome video footage of the attack,
perpetrated by a large Siberian tiger.
Bystanders also witnessed the attack.
Authorities have not shed any light as to why the man
was inside the enclosure in the first place.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
